newsitem.title: USA: Little economic impact seen from UPS stike - Parry.
newsitem.headline: Little economic impact seen from UPS stike - Parry.

text.p: President of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco Robert Parry said he expected little economic impact from the strike at United Parcel Service (UPS), the nation's largest package delivery service.

"I'm not expecting that this is a situation that is going to have a significant effect on the measures of performance of the U.S. economy," Parry said in response to a question following an address to the Northwest Taxable Bond Club.
Turning the the U.S. Treasury market and the four-point- plus drop experienced by the benchmark 30-year bond over the last week, Parry said he could not fully comprehend the market's recent behavior.
"I don't fully understand why the bond market has moved so much recently, particularly in the last couple days. The bond market has a fair amount of volatility," Parry told reporters.
In addition, the San Francisco Fed chief said July economic data were not enough to conclude the economy was gaining momentum at the start of the third quarter.

"The numbers that we've received about the economy's performance in July suggest that maybe we've had a little bit of a pickup, but I think that information is much too vague at this point to reach the conclusion that the economy is picking up steam," he added.
